first_comment: Bonus: just before the strike, she turned to him and asked, 'What if we get struck by lightning?' Minutes later it happened. Would you have kept hiking or turned back? ⚡

stories.headline: Lightning stopped his heart. She restarted it twice
stories.summary: A lightning strike's ground current hit a couple on a forest hike. Eva gave Nick CPR for the 50 minutes rescuers needed to find them. After 3 days in hospital, he proposed.
stories.why: They're now married, and her local fire department gave her a lifesaving award.

stories.stat_label: years since the last one was found
stories.headline: A lost Viking-era church was found near Erik the Red's farm
stories.summary: Archaeologists studied a stone ruin for 20 years without proof. Then a grave facing east, the Christian way, confirmed it: the first new Norse church found in Greenland in over 60 years.
stories.why: It may be a church that medieval texts call the 'Church under the Sunny Mountains'.

stories.headline: 12 new species of 'living fossil' spiders were found in China
stories.summary: These trapdoor spiders still have 12 armour plates on their backs, a trait most spiders lost long ago. The finds lift their genus from 43 known species to 55.
stories.why: They belong to the oldest surviving branch of the spider family tree.

stories.stat_label: dog trained to sniff out 'sea vomit'
stories.headline: A rescue dog who sniffs out 'sea vomit' won Animal of the Year
stories.summary: Sgiath, a 6-year-old Labrador, swapped mountain rescue for the coast. She smells out an invasive sea squirt nicknamed 'sea vomit' and has found hundreds of colonies.
stories.why: Finding invaders early by nose is faster and cheaper than lab tests.

fun_fact: When Sgiath finds sea vomit, she doesn't bark: she freezes and stares at it.
